newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 7.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* A survey says the U.S. economy will rebound from a sluggish second quarter to post at least one more year of healthy growth.
* Lockheed agreed to buy Northrop for $8.26 billion in stock.
* In the first half of 1997, merger activity rose to $366 billion in announced U.S. deals.
* H&R Block is waiting for better offers for its 80 percent stake in CompuServe.
* Mississippi is the first state to seal a settlement with the nation's cigarette makers.
* Ford outperformed its Big Three rivals in June.
* Junk Bond issuance topped $46 billion in 1997's first half.
* Sony 's Hollywood Studio has its first big summer hit in years with "Men in Black.
* Two Barney's creditos have agreed to put up a big slice of the retailers bankruptcy financing.
* BAA agreed to buy Duty Free International for about $674 million.
* France is giving up trying to meet the 3 percent budget deficit criterion this year for joining Europe's planned unified currency.
* Germany's Veba agreed to buy Wyle Electronics .
* Kellog and the Post division of Kraft are mum on whether they will follow last week's 2.6 percent cerial price markup by general mills.
* Russia's stock market still appears to have room to grow.
* Mario Gabelli, for at least 10 months, has been shopping a 25 percent stake in his money management firm.
* A factor behind the surge in junk bonds is the popularity of the collatoralized bond obligation, or CBO.
